data.title: Identity and future knowledge
data.description: Vincent gains time-travel powers at age nineteen in 2025 and operates in the past as Adam Pleskot. His foreknowledge remains secret.

data.title: Investment advantage concealed by analysis
data.description: Foreknowledge drives unusually successful investments; data analysis and prediction algorithms provide a public explanation.

data.title: Compete for the personal-computing standard
data.description: Compete with IBM, present products at NCC from 1978 and COMDEX from 1979 onward, and manufacture at the maximum feasible scale to achieve standard-setting market coverage.

data.title: Build a complete platform
data.description: Develop customer trust and a loyal network of users, software developers and peripheral manufacturers through integrated hardware, software, training and support.

data.title: Separate future-equipped facility
data.description: A secret facility outside the three companies uses equipment brought from the 2020s for chip design and lithography.

data.title: Changed availability of historical personnel
data.description: Gordon Letwin never joins Microsoft; Tim Paterson never develops QDOS or becomes available to Microsoft in this timeline.

data.title: Engineering and manufacturing organization buildout
data.description: Hire staff, establish software-development environments, computer manufacturing and R&D, and a conservative semiconductor operation.

data.title: Other companies monitor the market
data.description: Actively monitor Logix/AION without significant decisions or actions yet.

data.title: US personal-computer market expansion
data.description: Contribute through product availability, computer popularization, seamless peripherals and accessible interfaces.

outcomes.description: US personal-computer market is larger than in the base scenario.

data.title: Open platform and independent suppliers
data.description: Logix alone develops the Apple II and S-100 expansion cards; these demonstrate Adam’s ecosystem intentions and are not DRI obligations. Apple cards expose FlexiBUS and video to native Apple software. CP/M-6502 is deferred, with no product, schedule or cost commitment. Published interfaces and affordable developer access permit competing software, cards, peripherals and monitors. AION retains Abacus, C tools, Business Tools, AIONix and the existing Pulse offering; DRI licenses CP/M independently. BPI operates independently under its own brand from the cooperation period. Any further ownership separation around 1985 remains a future transaction, not the beginning of operational independence or a completed buyout.

data.title: Flexible independent clone manufacturing
data.description: Five partners begin preparation in January 1981 for a January 1982 coordinated launch. They retain their brands and may build mainboards, contract manufacture or buy Logix boards; buy custom chips from AION or qualified SGS; source qualified RAM freely; design local chassis/keyboards; and buy conforming monitors from Logix or others. Anything outside an initial range may be supplied by Logix or third parties, with clear warranty and integration ownership. No partner must manufacture a complete catalogue.

data.title: Common platform with country-specific editions
data.description: AION Software delivers and maintains German, French and Spanish CP/M/TUI, AIONix, Business Tools, Abacus and programming environments, coordinating underlying OS rights and release approval with independent DRI. Use common APIs, document formats and shared cores with local resources. Validate keyboards, accents, fonts, printing, sorting, numbers, currency and dates. Clone manufacturers separately license other publishers including WordStar, dBASE and BPI; statutory accounting/payroll adaptation requires separate local qualification. UK English editions and support serve Aion Tech. Localisation is not a national software fork.

data.title: Partner launch and forecast reconciliation
data.description: These agreements, preparations and January 1982 launches are accepted narrative additions. Existing ecosystem projections already include North Star and Vector; replace their unsigned-prospect assumptions in the next numerical reassessment, never add their sales twice. Germany, France, Spain and Aion Tech require country forecasts. No automatic sales multiplier is awarded for the launch. Transfer funding, localisation, pilot lots, marketing, Academy staffing, working capital and chip capacity must be costed before a revised investment/ROI claim; The 1981–1983 numerical planning reassessment is recorded in sales_reassessment_inputs.json, sales_forecast.json and roi_1974_1980.json; provisional transfer prices and capacity allowances are not signed contract terms. Aion Tech ownership and consolidation remain open.

data.title: Independent second-source production
data.description: SGS receives a non-exclusive independent manufacture-and-sale licence for ERAv1 and all agreed custom controllers, including MMU, system, bus, storage, network and video controllers. Each part and speed grade qualifies separately. ERAv1 stays on 3 µm; no shrink is implied. Preserve existing SMC rights. AION provides launch supply for parts not yet qualified at SGS, so January clone delivery does not depend on simultaneous qualification of the entire portfolio.

data.title: Fund the complete Autodesk development capability
data.description: Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective. Non-exclusive funded development. Autodesk retains its software ownership and cross-platform business; clear the underlying Interact contribution/porting rights with the founders, including Mike Riddle. Logix supplies distribution and joint marketing, without a source buyout or forced platform exclusivity. Professional 17-inch/800x600 hardware becomes available around June, not January. See team_development_program.json for deployment and acceptance requirements. Sponsorship is incremental project work, not counted as retail Team Edition sales. The 1981–1983 reassessment includes an explicit planning provision for sponsorship and conditional CAD demand; see sales_reassessment_inputs.json. This is not a contractual funding ceiling, supplier quotation or confirmed shipment count.

data.title: ERA² / Athena NCC 1983 planning baseline
data.description: Athena base: 2 × 128 KiB 2 µm 4164 modules and 5 MB HDD. Server: 4 × 256 KiB modules and 20 MB HDD. Both: ERA², 64 KiB graphics, one 5.25-inch DS/DD FDD, NIC and EEPROM BIOS; no ROM cards. AIONix 2 specification pending. All ERA² architectural numbers are engineering targets, with 16 MHz a stretch bin. AION Labs alone manufactures ERA² initially; SGS-ATES excluded for at least 12–18 months after initial commercial availability. Development dates are provisional; cost and financial forecasts remain unchanged.
